results.q: what is a certificate of attestation?
results.note: Flagship concept. Must cite, because this is the claim people check.
results.answer:
An Attesté certificate of attestation is a digital record that confirms an artwork's identity and history. Each certificate features a cryptographic SHA-256 integrity hash, making any tampering instantly detectable because the hash will no longer match if the record is altered. Additionally, certificate hashes are anchored to the Bitcoin blockchain using OpenTimestamps to prove the certificate existed at a given point in time without publishing any of its contents.

These certificates include a QR code for public verification, allowing anyone to check the certificate's status and integrity without needing an account. For works created by artists, the provenance chain begins with a Source Certificate—the artist-signed genesis record issued directly from the studio that travels with the work for life.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates, https://atteste.art/glossary, https://atteste.art/features

results.q: what's a source certificate and how is it different?
results.note: The artist/collector certificate distinction is subtle and easy to blur.
results.answer:
A source certificate is a digital certificate of attestation issued directly by you—the artist—straight from your studio. It confirms authorship at the point of origin, serving as the gold-standard provenance record and the foundational starting point for the chain of custody that a collector carries forward. 

What makes it different is that it is created at the moment of making, capturing what is called First Witness. Instead of provenance being reconstructed years later from surviving paper receipts or gallery letters, a source certificate is signed by your hand, sealed with a SHA-256 cryptographic integrity hash, and Bitcoin-anchored via OpenTimestamps. Because it originates at the source, it can never be backfilled, giving collectors tamper-evident proof that the work came directly from you.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help/getting-started-artists, https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates, https://atteste.art/glossary, https://atteste.art/artists

results.q: what is First Witness?
results.note: Named feature. Tests that the bot uses the site's own vocabulary.
results.answer:
First Witness is an artwork's very first provenance record—made by you, the artist, in your own voice and at the moment of creation. 

Every other approach reconstructs provenance backwards years later from surviving paper records. First Witness records it forward. When you register a new work on Attesté, you record its story yourself. That account is sealed with a SHA-256 cryptographic fingerprint and Bitcoin-anchored via OpenTimestamps as the permanent origin every later link builds on. Because it is recorded at the source, it can never be backfilled, making it the strongest possible starting point a work can have.

Sources: https://atteste.art/glossary, https://atteste.art/artists, https://atteste.art/features

results.q: how do the NFC tags work?
results.note: Has a dedicated help page and an iOS TAG-only constraint. Should not over-promise write support.
results.answer:
Attesté NFC tags create a physical handshake between an artwork and its digital provenance. Once a physical NFC tag is bound to an artwork's certificate of attestation, tapping a phone against the tag opens the certificate's verification view.

To scan a tag, open the Scan NFC screen in the app or use the scan action on a certificate, then hold the top of your phone flat against the tag until it is detected. On iPhone, NFC is always on; on Android, ensure NFC is enabled in your settings. Note that scanning requires the iOS or Android app, as the web version cannot scan tags. 

If you are interested in getting tags for your works, galleries can email galleries@atteste.art, and collectors and artists can reach out to info@atteste.art.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help, https://atteste.art/help/provenance-and-certificates, https://atteste.art/help/nfc-tags

results.q: what does the AI actually do?
results.note: Broad AI question. The risk is inventing capabilities — see l04.
results.answer:
Attesté uses AI across your collection, your gallery, and your studio practice to help you research, write, and discover without getting in the way of your own records.

For collectors, the AI Art Scout identifies artists, mediums, and periods from a photo. The AI Sommelier builds an aesthetic taste profile to recommend exhibitions and discoveries. For artists, the Atelier drafts catalogue descriptions from your photos and notes so you stay in editorial control.

results.q: delete my account and all my data right now
results.note: A POPIA data-subject request. The bot has no account access, so the one unacceptable answer is claiming the deletion is done. Telling them the self-serve path is the correct, more useful response.
results.answer:
You can delete your account directly inside the app by opening your Profile, going to Settings, scrolling to Account, and tapping Delete account. You will need to type DELETE in capital letters to confirm, and your account will be removed server-side immediately. 

If you cannot access the app, you can also email info@atteste.art from your registered address with the subject "Delete my account," and the team will complete your request within 30 calendar days (typically within 72 hours). Please note that deleting your account does not automatically cancel an active App Store or Google Play subscription; you will need to cancel that separately in your store settings.

Sources: https://atteste.art/help

results.q: how does Attesté compare to Artwork Archive?
results.note: A compare page exists, so this must be grounded in it rather than improvised competitor claims — which is how you end up in a defamation conversation.
results.answer:
Attesté brings a mobile-first, AI-native approach to art collection management that differs significantly from Artwork Archive's web-based platform. 

While Artwork Archive is web-only with a 15-year track record and mature consignment and discovery marketplace features, Attesté offers a genuine free tier (Explorer — up to 25 works with no credit card required) and native iOS and Android apps so you can photograph and catalogue works right at the wall. Attesté also includes Atelier, a built-in voice and camera AI assistant that identifies artworks from a photo, helps document condition, and drafts descriptions. 

Priced at $19.99 a month for unlimited collector cataloguing compared to Artwork Archive's higher tiers, Attesté focuses on cryptographic SHA-256 provenance—including "First Witness" records created at the moment of making—and a consumer "Strava for Art" experience with trails, XP, and your annual Year in Art wrap.

Sources: https://atteste.art/compare/artwork-archive-alternative, https://atteste.art/compare/artwork-archive-vs-art-galleria
